findings.text: cli.help.argument says `init` refuses any argument (row `init --json`) with exit status 2 and writes nothing, and cli.help says arguments are read before anything else. install.init.repository still matches every run of `init` in a directory: with `.git` present it takes every installed file, and without it it writes the not-a-root message. So for `init --json` the two rules require different outcomes. install.version.output got `Provided <arguments> is empty` / `Otherwise → cli.help.argument`; install.init.repository got no such change.

The contract `system.cli.init` does not say that `init` takes no argument, but cli.help.argument now refuses every argument to it. The changed `system.cli.version` and the new `cli.cli.help` both say this; `system.cli.init` was not changed and is not a candidate. Its exit status 2 ('the command could not run') covers a refusal only loosely.

cli.help.argument refuses a misused baseline command with one line on stderr and says it checks and writes nothing, but baseline.run.lint's When ('someone runs manifest, diff, impact, pack, judge or verify') is not narrowed to runs whose arguments were accepted: in a tree with a lint error it writes lint's text instead, and in a clean tree it lets the run go on, so 'manifest --json' writes the manifest through baseline.manifest.write, and 'judge --json', 'diff --since HEAD~1 --bogus' go on through baseline.judge.input, baseline.diff.since and baseline.diff.baseline. Only cli.help's Rationale says the arguments are read first, and Rationale is not behaviour.

lint.run.root applies whenever someone runs `lint` in a directory, whatever its arguments. For `lint --since HEAD~1` it requires lint to go on reading the spec tree, or to write that no spec root was found. cli.help.argument requires the same run to write one line naming `lint` and `--since`, and to check and write nothing else. The rule that arguments are read before anything else appears only in the Rationale of cli.help, so no element decides which rule wins.

baseline.diff.since starts on 'someone runs diff with diff.since, or pack with pack.since', not limited to arguments the command takes. For `diff --since HEAD~1 --bogus`, its Then (compare with HEAD~1) and cli.help.argument's Otherwise (refuse, check nothing) both apply and cannot both hold.

baseline.judge.input starts on 'someone runs judge, giving it the input <input> on stdin', with no limit on arguments, though system.cli.judge now says judge takes no argument. For `judge --json` with a valid check_result, judge.input's Then (read it) and cli.help.argument's Otherwise (refuse, check and write nothing) both apply.

cli.help.argument reads whatever non-empty argument follows --since as its revision, so `diff --since --json` or `pack --since -h` hands "--json" or "-h" to baseline.diff.since as <revision>. No rule or Examples row says whether such a revision is refused as an argument or put to git, where it could read as an option rather than a commit; the guard "git knows <revision> as a commit" leaves this undecided.
